name: @otp/api
//: THERE IS NO "exports" MAP HERE AND THERE MUST NOT BE ONE. This is load-bearing, not an omission.
The two live leaderboard routes are apps/game/api/score.ts and apps/game/api/top.ts, and they reach
this package by deep path -- '@otp/api/src/deps.ts' and '@otp/api/src/handlers.ts'. A package with no
exports map is the only kind whose arbitrary subpaths resolve at all; the moment one is added, every
subpath not named in it stops existing. Measured 2026-10-21 by adding the ordinary well-meaning map
{ ".": "./src/index.ts" } and running both resolvers: node answers ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED,
"Package subpath './src/deps.ts' is not defined by exports", and tsc answers four TS2307s, one per
import across the two files. That is the ENTIRE leaderboard surface failing at once, and before
apps/game/tsconfig.api.json existed it would have failed in silence -- those two files were typechecked
by nothing, so a dead board would have reached production and waited for someone to notice.
If you need an entry point, add a plain 'main' or let callers keep using the deep path. If you add an
exports map anyway, it must name './src/*' explicitly, and `pnpm typecheck` is what will tell you.
The '.ts' extension on those imports is load-bearing for the same reason -- see apps/game/api/top.ts.
